newsitem.title: USA: A.T. Cross sees flat sales, lower earnings.
newsitem.headline: A.T. Cross sees flat sales, lower earnings.

text.p: A.T. Cross Co said Thursday it expects flat sales and lower earnings for the year after reporting third quarter earnings that were down 41 percent from the year-ago figure.
The maker of fine writing instruments reported third quarter earnings of $0.10 per share, compared to the year-ago figure of $0.17.
"It is now apparent that sales for the year will be approximately flat and earnings will be down," the company said.
The company said the fourth quarter traditionally generates 35 percent of the year's sales.

"Although the slight decline in our third quarter writing instrument sales is disappointing, we continue to see sales growth in our new product lines -- Townsend, Solo Classic and Metropolis -- but not at the level we anticipated," stated company Chief Executive Russell Boss.

"Our ability to more rapidly expand distribution and sales of our new products has been hampered by retailers' reluctance to increase inventory levels of writing instruments in anticipation of consumer demand."
The company said that increasing the variety in its product lines is a long-term initiative that won't provide significant return over the next few years.
